bull_bear.body:
- Over 92 years of legacy, brand trust and reliability as one of India's established building-solutions companies
- Nationwide distribution network of 14,000+ dealer outlets and sales depots reaching 1,00,000+ villages and 600+ cities
- International presence and export footprint across 35+ countries
- Premiumisation strategy (Evercool) driving differentiated, higher-value roofing sales, with Evercool volumes growing 44% in FY26
- Multi-segment building-solutions ecosystem across roofing, boards & panels and PEB, positioned as an integrated 'system solutions' provider rather than a single-product manufacturer
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Raw material price volatility (chrysotile fibre, cement, steel) — These are the Company's primary raw materials; price fluctuations directly impact profitability, and the Company can only pass through increases to customers to a limited extent.
- Concentrated, geopolitically-exposed sourcing of chrysotile fibre and wood pulp — Both inputs are sourced from a limited number of global suppliers; the ongoing Israel-Iran conflict poses an ongoing risk to consistent supply of these critical raw materials.
- Steel price volatility for the PEB/ESBS segment — Steel, the primary raw material for PEB manufacturing, saw a sharp price increase late in FY26 driven by global geopolitical uncertainty, supply-chain disruption and energy-cost concerns, pressuring segment costs.
- Rupee depreciation raising imported input costs — Depreciation of the Indian Rupee against the US Dollar raised the cost of imported roofing inputs, placing significant pressure on segment profitability during the year, particularly in H2 FY26.
- Global geopolitical and trade-policy uncertainty — Escalating tensions (including the Middle East conflict) and unpredictable US tariff policy create volatility in energy/commodity prices and global supply chains, with adverse knock-on effects on household purchasing power and construction activity.
- Climate and monsoon variability affecting seasonal demand — Uneven monsoons and climate-related disruptions affect construction activity and seasonal demand, particularly in the rural and semi-urban markets that are core to the Roofing business.
- Execution risk in government-driven affordable housing demand — While affordable-housing demand (e.g. PMAY) is expected to be large, execution risk around delivery timelines, land-acquisition delays and skilled-labour shortages could moderate the pace of construction activity that drives the Company's core markets.
- Price-sensitive, mature, competitive core roofing market — The Indian fibre-cement roofing industry (~43-44 lakh MT p.a.) is largely flat and mature, with a highly price-sensitive customer base and rising competition from alternative (non-AC/metal) roofing categories, constraining pricing power and growth.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: Everest Industries manufactures and sells building materials across three segments: fibre-cement roofing sheets, boards & panels (dry-construction wall/ceiling systems), and pre-engineered steel buildings (PEB/ESBS). Its products serve residential, commercial, institutional and industrial customers through a nationwide dealer/distribution network as well as export markets.
business.title: What they do

business.body:
- **Roofing:** Asbestos Cement (AC) roofing sheets, Evercool premium cool-roof sheets, Supercolour
- **Boards & Panels:** Everest Fibre Cement Boards, Everest Heavy Duty Boards, Everest Rapicon Walls, framing systems, fasteners, jointing compounds
- **Pre-Engineered Steel Buildings (ESBS/PEB):** Everest Smart Steel Buildings
business.title: Products & brands

business.body:
- Falak Investment Private Limited — related party: Holding company
- Everest Building Products, Mauritius — subsidiary: Wholly owned (100%) subsidiary
- Everestind FZE, United Arab Emirates — subsidiary: Wholly owned subsidiary of Everest Building Products, Mauritius (itself a wholly owned subsidiary of the Company)
- Everest Buildpro Private Limited — subsidiary: Wholly owned (100%) subsidiary; operates the Mysore plant (Boards & Panels)
- Everest Steel Building Private Limited — subsidiary: Wholly owned (100%) subsidiary; has not yet commenced operations

business.title: Group structure (subsidiaries / JV / related parties)

business.body:
- Over 92 years of legacy, brand trust and reliability as one of India's established building-solutions companies
- Nationwide distribution network of 14,000+ dealer outlets and sales depots reaching 1,00,000+ villages and 600+ cities
- International presence and export footprint across 35+ countries
- Premiumisation strategy (Evercool) driving differentiated, higher-value roofing sales, with Evercool volumes growing 44% in FY26
- Multi-segment building-solutions ecosystem across roofing, boards & panels and PEB, positioned as an integrated 'system solutions' provider rather than a single-product manufacturer
business.title: Competitive strengths

outlook.body:
- Roofing: sharper geographical prioritisation (market clustering) of markets to enhance logistical efficiencies, service responsiveness and a leaner sales deployment model
- Roofing: premiumisation of the portfolio (Evercool) as a core strategic priority, alongside a digital influencer loyalty programme to deepen channel engagement and demand generation
- Roofing: proactive pricing corrections taken in H2 FY26 to offset inflationary cost pressures, continuing focus on cost optimisation and margin recovery
- Boards & Panels: shift from traditional construction materials to new-age, lightweight dry-construction systems; solidify industry leadership via category creation and system-solution selling (products + technical expertise + execution support)
- Boards & Panels: expand integrated system offering (insulation, jointing tapes and other completion components) and invest in contractor skilling/certification to ensure standardised installation
- ESBS/PEB: renewed focus on rebuilding execution capabilities, improving order quality and margins, and building a resilient project pipeline in carefully selected strategic markets ahead of a planned scale-up
- Dividend is governed by a Board-approved Dividend Distribution Policy (per SEBI Listing Regulation 43A) and the Company describes its practice as continuing a 'past track record' of paying a final dividend, having recommended one (subject to AGM approval) even in a loss-making year. No amount was transferred to General Reserves during FY 2025-26. Paid-up equity capital rose marginally during the year solely from allotment of shares under the Employees Stock Option Scheme - 2021; no other equity, warrant or sweat-equity issuance occurred.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Everest's expansion has historically proceeded through named-site commissioning: a greenfield plant at Lakhmapur, Maharashtra (2008), added Boards capacity at Roorkee, Uttarakhand (2010), a Steel Buildings (PEB) facility at Dahej, Gujarat (2012), and, most recently, the Mysore plant commissioned 'in record time' in 2024 (operated through subsidiary Everest Buildpro Private Limited). In FY 2025-26 the focus shifted from new capacity toward stabilising and ramping up this recently-added Southern manufacturing footprint: the Boards & Panels business reported that 'the stabilisation of our South manufacturing facility has enhanced our ability to serve key markets with greater speed and efficiency,' contributing to over 30% growth in Rapicon sales in the South. No new greenfield or brownfield project with a stated commissioning/completion timeline was disclosed for FY27 in the routed text; the Company instead described FY26 as a 'Transformation agenda with Renewed focus on System & Solution Selling' rather than a capacity-expansion year.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- India's economic outlook for FY27 seen as positive, with real GDP growth projected at 6.8-7.2% and domestic consumption/rising real incomes as the primary growth engine
- Record infrastructure capex (budgeted at Rs. 12.2 lakh crore for FY27) expected to provide strong demand visibility for the construction and building materials sectors
- GST 2.0 rationalisation expected to reduce construction costs and lower housing prices, boosting demand in affordable and mid-segment housing
- Trade diversification via recently concluded FTAs (UK, EU) and active US negotiations seen as offering upside for export-oriented building material sectors
- Roofing: Indian fibre-cement roofing industry (~43-44 lakh MT p.a.) remained largely flat in FY26 (~1% growth); long-term outlook stable on rural/semi-urban demand and government housing programmes (PMAY), though the market remains price-sensitive with rising alternative-roofing competition
- Boards & Panels: industry (~1 million MT, ~Rs. 1,800 crore) expected to grow at 10-12% CAGR over the next 5-7 years, driven by urbanisation, green-building initiatives, data-centre construction and adoption of dry-construction systems
- ESBS/PEB: industry projected to grow at ~12% CAGR over the next 5 years, driven by industrialisation, warehousing/logistics, renewable energy, and government initiatives (industrial corridors, Make in India)
- Risk: escalating geopolitical tensions (Middle East conflict) and US tariff dynamics pose material input-cost and supply-chain risk for energy-intensive segments (steel, cement)
- Risk: rupee depreciation against the US Dollar increased the cost of imported roofing inputs and pressured industry profitability during the year
- Risk: uneven monsoons, climate-related disruptions, and execution risk around PMAY delivery timelines, land acquisition delays and skilled-labour shortages could moderate the pace of construction activity
- ESBS/PEB business remained focussed on securing sustainable and profitable orders within carefully selected strategic markets and segments, and on building a resilient project pipeline aligned with long-term growth objectives, despite a short-term revenue decline
- Boards & Panels specification-led sales (via business development teams working with architects, consultants and developers) grew significantly across 11 focus markets during the year
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: An established Indian building-solutions company spanning roofing, boards & panels, and pre-engineered steel buildings, serving homes, institutions and industries across India and 35+ export markets.

open.item: Board recommended a final dividend of Re. 1/- per equity share (10% of face value Rs. 10) for FY 2025-26, subject to shareholder approval at the AGM.
Following cost reduction, pricing actions and one-time provisioning in FY26, the Company is well positioned to be profitable in FY 2026-27.
ESBS/PEB division's FY26 topline decline was a deliberate step to rebuild execution capabilities in order to scale up in FY 2026-27.
ESBS/PEB division targets scaling up execution capabilities and growing topline in FY 2026-27 after a deliberate strategic pull-back in FY26.
Company is well positioned to be profitable in FY 2026-27 following pricing, productivity and cost-structure actions taken in H2 FY26.

The Company has identified seven Must Win Battles (Quality, Service, Price, Value Added Sales, Cost, Productivity and Volume) supported by standardised Ways of Working, as the basis for a sustained (not one-time) performance turnaround.
Sharper geographical prioritisation (market clustering) of Roofing markets, expected to enhance logistical efficiencies, service responsiveness and enable a leaner sales deployment model.
Premiumisation of the roofing portfolio (Evercool) to remain a core strategic priority to enhance customer value and margin.

Boards & Panels to expand its integrated system offering (insulation, jointing tapes and other completion components) and invest in contractor skilling/certification to solidify category leadership in dry construction.
Company has contracted but not yet executed capital-account commitments of Rs. 155.45 lakhs (net of advances) as at March 31, 2026.
